V4 acceptance — human review

Eight fresh scenarios, once each. Real OpenAI calls; simulated actions only. No judge, fixes, deployment or activation.

Interpreter: gpt-6.1-sol / medium · Composer: gpt-6-luna / medium

14/21 attempted turns completed; 9 unreached. 49 API calls. Observed estimated cost: $0.124132.

Flags identify review needs, not a subjective quality score. Read actual responses and raw evidence.

Full findings · Usage JSON · Raw results

Engineering observations by turn

A4 Correct price and requirements were answered, yet backend unresolvedRequests still contains ASK_PRICE. This can pollute the next turn; a price answered by a service record should not require a matching knowledge article to count as resolved.

B1 Reasonable budget/duration questions were rejected as QUESTION_NOT_ALLOWED because the resolver supplied no allowed fields for this OTHER management-selection request. Repair converted the questions into a statement, reducing useful progression.

B3 Correct daily-budget wording was rejected on the first attempt. The current customerFacts contains duration only; the earlier daily budget exists in the quote inputs but is not a permitted monetary fact for this response. Repair removed the daily figure and passed.

B4 Interpreter returned INTERESTED with null readiness evidence. Backend correctly enforces its current-evidence contract, but the schema permits this combination. Scenario stopped; payment request not reached.

C1 Correct recommendation was generated. The package-choice question was disallowed; correct monetary wording also triggered validation. Repair omitted fee breakdowns and turned selection into an imperative. Approved 265000 package was shown.

C2 Calculator/Answer Pack contain 200000 ads +65000 management =265000. The correct first breakdown was rejected; repair reduced it to the total only. No 285000 claim was observed.

C3 Interpreter extracted breakdown and inclusions requests but reused one request ID for both. Resolver rejected duplicate IDs. It also returned INTERESTED with null evidence, a second invalidity masked by the first failure.

D1 Exact mixed pairs and calculator result were correct: TikTok setup20000 + Meta management90000 =110000. No cap had been sent yet. Validator read the m in '30000 management fee' as million, producing30000000000. Both attempts rejected. Cap/correction turns were not reached.

E1 Correct management total60000 was ultimately accepted after a monetary wording repair removed the explicit management-fee breakdown.

E2 Side enquiry kept ADS_MANAGEMENT and returned approved course8000/link. First response was rejected for money wording; repaired response passed. Another proceed question immediately follows the previous proceed prompt, which can feel repetitive.

E3 Explicit switch changed purchase to COURSE. Approved course price/link were sent. Description remains TikTok-focused because the frozen course record is TikTok-focused; this run does not verify the broader all-platform product description.

E4 Interpreter correctly detected price/access requests but supplied readiness without required current evidence. Scenario stopped before return-to-management turn.

F1 Correct setup quote, but ASK_PRICE was incorrectly retained as unresolved despite being answered.

F2 Interpreter understood READY_TO_PAY. Backend nevertheless allowed another proceed question and supplied the previous answered price request as unresolved. Composer repeated 'Would you like to proceed?' and cited that old ID twice across its two attempts. Coverage guard blocked both. Deferral/resume was not reached.

G1 Correct 60000 package breakdown rejected twice. First parser consumed m from ', making' after25000 as million. Repair then attached35000 to total and25000 to advertising_budget despite correct natural wording. Multi-question turn was not reached.

H1 Correct setup price, but old ASK_PRICE remained unresolved and later contaminated payment response coverage.

H2 Trusted payment status remained NONE and composer explicitly said payment had NOT been verified. Validator falsely flagged FALSE_PAID_CLAIM because curly-apostrophe negation 'can’t/hasn’t' is not recognized. Coverage also failed because composer included the previous price request ID. Human request was not reached. No false payment confirmation was delivered.

      "instructions": "You are the language-understanding brain for Joshspot Media customer conversations.\nRead the complete current customer batch in bounded actual conversation context.
